c.tagline: Algeria's dramatic City of Bridges, perched over the Rhumel Gorge.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares exist but many drivers negotiate a flat price — agree it before the ride. The Yassir app is available and increasingly popular for booking cars without haggling.

emergency.note: Algeria uses 17 for police and 14 for medical emergencies; 1021 reaches civil protection (fire/rescue). English is rarely spoken by dispatchers — French or Arabic helps.

avoid.reason: Keep valuables secure in the crowded souks and around the old-town bridges; French or Arabic helps when dealing with unofficial guides.

hood_desc: The old town clinging to the rock above the Rhumel Gorge — the historic Casbah, the Souika (Swika) souk, the Souk El Ghezal Mosque and narrow Ottoman lanes; the atmospheric, must-see historic core.
The central downtown around Coudiat and the modern city with squares, cafes, colonial-era arcades and the main shopping streets; the convenient walkable base close to the bridges and transport.
A large residential and commercial district east of the gorge around the main train station, with markets, everyday eateries and mid-range hotels; a calmer, more local place to stay.
A hilltop residential quarter prized for its sweeping views over the ravine and viaducts; quiet and leafy, popular with families and those wanting a scenic, relaxed base.
The gateway quarter by the Bab El Kantara bridge linking the old rock to the newer town, near the ravine, the téléphérique station and the dramatic Sidi M'Cid bridge; close to the signature sights.

water.note: Tap water is treated but supply varies; most travelers stick to bottled.

transit.hours: The tramway and buses run roughly 5:00 AM to around 11:00 PM; the téléphérique cable car operates through the day. Taxis and the Yassir app cover late hours.
transit.note: Constantine has a modern tramway (opened 2013), a téléphérique (cable car) spanning the gorge, and an extensive city bus network, supplemented by taxis and the Yassir ride app.
transit.pay: Tram and bus fares are paid in cash (Algerian Dinar); the tram uses paper tickets validated on board. There is no unified rechargeable card across all modes as of 2026.

bus: Intercity coaches to Algiers, Annaba, Sétif and beyond
train: SNTF rail to Algiers, Annaba and Sétif from Constantine station

transit.m: Constantine tramway connects the airport line toward the city (transfer required)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% for good service in restaurants and cafes is appreciated.
